newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa Cargo sees 3pct truck growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo sees 3pct truck growth in 97.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it expected its air cargo road trucking volumes to rise by about three percent this year.
Hartmut Flessa, the airline's road and rail manager, told Reuters: "The cargo volumes are not developing so strongly this year. We estimate trucking growth of about three percent this year."
Lufthansa Cargo trucked some 350,000 tonnes of cargo between Frankfurt and European destinations last year, Flessa said.
The airline registered 63,000 airport to airport truck trips in 1996 and 58,115 in 1995, representing an average load factor of six tonnes per truck.
Within Germany, the Lufthansa trucks carried up to eight tonnes on average which meant they were effectively full due to the cargo volumes, Flessa added.

In a Reuters interview, Hans Driedger, general manager capacity management, said that demand for airfreight road feeder services (RFS) was rising due to centralisation on the airline's Frankfurt cargo hub.
Lufthansa trucked a high percentage of its European air cargo to and from Frankfurt since passenger aircraft serving continental destinations had only a small cargo capacity, he explained.
Lufthansa trucked by far the largest share of all trucked air cargo passing through Frankfurt airport, although no absolute figures were available, he added.
Driedger said about 40 trucking companies were contracted for three years to provide scheduled RFS services for Lufthansa at agreed, long-term prices.
The current contracts ran until July 1999 but new deals could be made before then if LCAG decided to start new scheduled RFS routes.
For ad-hoc needs, the regular 40 truckers and a further 30 suppliers were used, he added. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017
